Let’s dive into Chapter Five: Designing Products and Services That Create Impact and Income.
Now that your platforms are set, it’s time to turn your passion for helping others into a thriving business. This is where things really get interesting—where sharing advice shifts from just getting your message out there, to building offerings that actually solve problems and make a real difference.
So, what kinds of products and services do experts usually create? Well, there’s a whole range—from books and guides, to online courses and workshops, even live seminars or group events. Some experts offer personal coaching or consulting, membership sites with ongoing programs, or simple digital resources like templates and checklists.
But here’s where it gets crucial: the process starts by tuning in to your audience. What are they struggling with? What do they keep asking about? Listening to their feedback, spotting those recurring challenges, and just asking them directly—this is how you’ll uncover what people are actually searching for.
The best products don’t just sound good—they address a specific pain point, or help someone achieve a clear result.
To make this easier, imagine your offerings as a value ladder. At the bottom, you’ve got free or low-cost resources—maybe a quick guide or a handful of helpful videos. These build trust and introduce people to your style. As folks start seeing results and getting to know you, they might climb up to more in-depth options—like a mini-course, a group program, or even working with you one-on-one.
Let’s put it in context. Your value ladder could start with a free article or video packed with practical tips. Next, you could offer an affordable ebook or a bite-sized course with step-by-step solutions. For those who want more accountability and support, maybe a group coaching program. And for people looking for tailored advice, a premium consulting package.
Every step is designed to help your audience move closer to their goals, while giving them choices that fit their needs and budget.
Now, here’s something to pay attention to: quality matters. If you promise a result, deliver on it. Make your instructions clear, check in with your clients, and support them along the way. Happy customers become your biggest advocates—they’ll spread the word and bring new people to you.
There’s also the question of pricing. This trips up a lot of new experts. Maybe you worry that charging for your advice feels selfish, or that people will see you differently. But here’s the truth: when someone pays for your product or service, they’re more likely to take it seriously and get real results. And, earning income means you can keep doing the work you love—helping even more people.
So, how do you make sure your offerings are both impactful and profitable?
Start by really understanding what your audience needs. Design your products to deliver clear, measurable outcomes. Offer a range of choices for different budgets and preferences. Always focus on quality and follow-through. And, set prices that reflect the value you provide and support the future of your business.
When you create products and services with care, intention, and heart, you’re not just building a business—you’re changing lives, including your own. Sharing your expertise becomes a way to make a meaningful impact, while also creating financial freedom and fulfillment.
